# Metric specs

```{r specs}
mediator_specs_adult <- list(
  list(name = "prox_strength",      posteriors = prox_posteriors,  field = "prox_strength"),
  list(name = "prox_degree",        posteriors = prox_posteriors,  field = "prox_degree"),
  list(name = "groom_out_strength", posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_strength"),
  list(name = "groom_in_strength",  posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_strength"),
  list(name = "groom_out_degree",   posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_out_degree"),
  list(name = "groom_in_degree",    posteriors = groom_posteriors, field = "groom_in_degree")
)

mediator_specs_juv <- list(
  list(name = "prox_strength_juv",      posteriors = prox_posteriors_juv,  field = "prox_strength_juv"),
  list(name = "prox_degree_juv",        posteriors = prox_posteriors_juv,  field = "prox_degree_juv"),
  list(name = "groom_out_strength_juv", posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_out_strength_juv"),
  list(name = "groom_in_strength_juv",  posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_in_strength_juv"),
  list(name = "groom_out_degree_juv",   posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_out_degree_juv"),
  list(name = "groom_in_degree_juv",    posteriors = groom_posteriors_juv, field = "groom_in_degree_juv")
)
```

```{r summarize-fn}
# If you already have summarize_network_draws() defined/sourced elsewhere in
# your project (e.g. script 5), delete this chunk and source that file instead
# so both scripts use the identical implementation.
summarize_network_draws <- function(draws) {
  tibble(
    estimate_mean   = mean(draws),
    estimate_median = median(draws),
    network_q025    = quantile(draws, 0.025, names = FALSE),
    network_q975    = quantile(draws, 0.975, names = FALSE),
    prop_positive   = mean(draws > 0),
    prop_negative   = mean(draws < 0)
  )
}
```

# Correlation function

Draw-matched correlation: for each posterior draw *k*, take every male's
juvenile-metric value and his post-dispersal-metric value, correlate across
males, and repeat over draws to build a posterior distribution of *r*.
Only males present in **both** posterior objects (tracked as juveniles,
dispersed, and re-tracked as adults) are included.

```{r correlation-function}
correlate_juvenile_post_dispersal <- function(adult_specs, juv_specs,
                                               num_draws = 1000,
                                               method = "pearson") {

  adult_names <- sapply(adult_specs, function(s) s$name)
  juv_names   <- sapply(juv_specs,   function(s) s$name)

  # match juvenile "X_juv" to adult "X"
  pairs <- list()
  for (jn in juv_names) {
    base_name <- sub("_juv$", "", jn)
    if (base_name %in% adult_names) {
      pairs[[base_name]] <- list(juv = jn, adult = base_name)
    } else {
      cat("No adult match found for '", jn, "' - skipping\n", sep = "")
    }
  }

  all_results <- list()
  all_pooled  <- list()

  for (pn in names(pairs)) {

    juv_spec   <- juv_specs[[which(juv_names == pairs[[pn]]$juv)]]
    adult_spec <- adult_specs[[which(adult_names == pairs[[pn]]$adult)]]

    cat("\n>>> Correlating", pairs[[pn]]$juv, "<->", pairs[[pn]]$adult, "\n")

    common_codes <- intersect(names(juv_spec$posteriors), names(adult_spec$posteriors))

    if (length(common_codes) < 10) {
      cat("  Too few males with both posteriors:", length(common_codes), "- skipping\n")
      next
    }
    cat("  n males =", length(common_codes), "\n")

    juv_draws_avail   <- length(juv_spec$posteriors[[common_codes[1]]][[juv_spec$field]])
    adult_draws_avail <- length(adult_spec$posteriors[[common_codes[1]]][[adult_spec$field]])
    draws_use <- min(num_draws, juv_draws_avail, adult_draws_avail)

    if (draws_use < num_draws) {
      cat("  Requested", num_draws, "draws but only", draws_use, "available - using", draws_use, "\n")
    }

    r_all <- numeric(draws_use)

    for (k in 1:draws_use) {
      juv_vals   <- sapply(common_codes, function(id) juv_spec$posteriors[[id]][[juv_spec$field]][k])
      adult_vals <- sapply(common_codes, function(id) adult_spec$posteriors[[id]][[adult_spec$field]][k])
      r_all[k] <- cor(juv_vals, adult_vals, method = method, use = "complete.obs")
    }

    res <- summarize_network_draws(r_all) %>%
      mutate(juvenile_metric       = pairs[[pn]]$juv,
             post_dispersal_metric = pairs[[pn]]$adult,
             n_males               = length(common_codes),
             num_draws             = draws_use,
             method                = method,
             .before = 1)

    cat(sprintf("  r mean = %6.3f  95%% CI [%6.3f, %6.3f]  pd = %4.1f%%\n",
                res$estimate_mean, res$network_q025, res$network_q975,
                max(res$prop_positive, res$prop_negative) * 100))

    all_results[[pn]] <- res
    all_pooled[[pn]]  <- r_all
  }

  list(summary = bind_rows(all_results), pooled = all_pooled)
}
```

# Run

```{r run-correlations}
corr_out <- correlate_juvenile_post_dispersal(
  mediator_specs_adult, mediator_specs_juv,
  num_draws = 1000,
  method = "pearson"   # switch to "spearman" if strength/degree are skewed
)

print(as.data.frame(corr_out$summary), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Plot: posterior distribution of each correlation

```{r plot-correlations, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
plot_data <- imap_dfr(corr_out$pooled, ~ tibble(pair = .y, r = .x))

# Map raw metric names to clean display labels
label_map <- c(
  "prox_strength"      = "Proximity strength",
  "prox_degree"        = "Proximity degree",
  "groom_out_strength" = "Groom out-strength",
  "groom_in_strength"  = "Groom in-strength",
  "groom_out_degree"   = "Groom out-degree",
  "groom_in_degree"    = "Groom in-degree"
)

plot_data$pair_label <- label_map[plot_data$pair]

# order facets by posterior mean r, most positive first
pair_order <- corr_out$summary %>%
  arrange(desc(estimate_mean)) %>%
  mutate(pair_label = label_map[post_dispersal_metric]) %>%
  pull(pair_label)

plot_data$pair_label <- factor(plot_data$pair_label, levels = pair_order)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = r, fill = pair_label)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, color = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~ pair_label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Correlation (r) between juvenile and post-dispersal metrics",
    y = "Density",
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "plain"))
```

grooming metrics show consistent, non-trivial positive continuity from juvenile to adult; proximity strength is null; proximity degree is negative.
grooming relationships seem to carry forward across the dispersal transition in a way proximity doesn't, and proximity degree even seems to invert.

# Correlation among maternal characteristics

```{r}

library(dplyr)

maternal_label_map <- c(
  "mother_avg_elo"              = "Maternal rank",
  "mom_groom_proportion"        = "Maternal grooming\ninvestment",
  "mom_prox_proportion"         = "Maternal proximity\ninvestment",
  "mom_groom_eigen_mean"        = "Mother grooming\neigen-centrality",
  "mom_prox_eigen_mean"         = "Mother proximity\neigen-centrality"
)

maternal_vars <- emigrants_full %>%
  select(all_of(names(maternal_label_map)))

# Rename columns to the clean labels BEFORE computing correlations, so
# the labels appear directly in the matrix/plot
names(maternal_vars) <- maternal_label_map[names(maternal_vars)]

cor_matrix <- cor(maternal_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

ggcorrplot::ggcorrplot(cor_matrix, type = "upper", lab = TRUE, lab_size = 3.5,
           colors = c("#C62828", "white", "#1565C0"),
           tl.cex = 11, tl.srt = 45) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5))

# Pairwise correlation matrix, handling missing data per pair (not
# requiring complete cases across all 7 variables at once, since sample
# sizes vary a lot by variable in this project)
cor_matrix <- cor(maternal_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")

print(round(cor_matrix, 2))

library(Hmisc)

cor_results <- rcorr(as.matrix(maternal_vars), type = "pearson")
cor_results$r  # correlation coefficients
cor_results$P  # p-values
cor_results$n  # sample size per pair (important given how much n varies here)

```

#Plot maternalmale ranks
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(RColorBrewer)

# ── Data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# x = maternal rank, y = male rank one year post-dispersal
# color = natal group (BirthGp), shape = immigration group (ImmigrationGp1)
plot_data <- emigrants_full %>%
  filter(!is.na(mother_avg_elo), !is.na(elo_one_year_male_male))

# ggplot's default shape scale only has 6 distinct values before it
# recycles/errors — expand it in case there are more than 6 immigration
# groups (BD, NH, AK, KB, LT, CR, IF = up to 7 in your data)
n_immig_groups <- n_distinct(plot_data$ImmigrationGp1)
shape_values   <- c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12)[seq_len(n_immig_groups)]

# Muted/pastel palette for natal group — Set2 is muted and colorblind-safe,
# with 8 distinct colors (RColorBrewer caps at 8 for qualitative palettes)
n_natal_groups <- n_distinct(plot_data$BirthGp)
natal_colors   <- brewer.pal(max(n_natal_groups, 3), "Set2")[seq_len(n_natal_groups)]

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = mother_avg_elo, y = elo_one_year_male_male)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = BirthGp, shape = ImmigrationGp1), size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_values) +
  scale_color_manual(values = natal_colors) +
  labs(
    x     = "Maternal rank during the juvenile period",
    y     = "Male rank one year post-dispersal",
    color = "Natal group",
    shape = "Immigration group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "right"
  )

print(p)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(data_dir, "maternal_vs_male_rank.png"),
  plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300
)
```
